The fluorescent lights of the office hummed with the same low-grade anxiety that had been building in Arthur’s chest since 9:00 AM. It was "Bring Your Pet to Work Day," a corporate initiative designed to boost morale by allowing employees to bring in creatures that were, statistically speaking, more likely to cause liability issues than to improve productivity.

Arthur had brought in Barnaby, a African Grey Parrot with a vocabulary that ranged from "Hello" to "Your mother is a hamster," depending on who was in the room. Barnaby sat in his travel cage on Arthur’s desk, preening a feather with an air of judicial detachment.

The trouble began at 10:15 AM.

Arthur’s boss, Mr. Henderson, was on a call in the glass-walled conference room. Arthur, trying to be helpful, had left his own phone on speaker while taking a sensitive call with the legal department regarding a merger. He had forgotten to mute it.

Barnaby tilted his head. His beak opened.

"Merger approved," the parrot squawked, in a perfect mimicry of Arthur’s voice.

Arthur froze. He looked at the conference room. Mr. Henderson was still talking, but he had stopped mid-sentence, his eyes wide as he stared at the parrot.

"Did you just say..." Henderson started, then trailed off.

Barnaby, sensing the tension, decided to escalate. "Confidential," he added, followed by a low whistle that sounded suspiciously like the sound of a safe combination being dialed.

Arthur scrambled. He lunged for the cage, but Barnaby was faster. The bird hopped onto the edge of the desk, flapped his wings, and landed on the back of Henderson’s chair.

"Insider trading!" Barnaby shrieked.

The office went silent. Every head turned. The printer, usually a source of rhythmic comfort, seemed to hold its breath.

Arthur’s mind raced. He had to stop this. He had to explain. He had to...

"Mr. Henderson," Arthur said, his voice cracking. "It’s a trick. He’s... he’s been watching too much news."

Henderson turned slowly. "Arthur, did your bird just quote the Q3 earnings projection?"

"No! He’s just... he’s very smart. He learned it from... from the radio!"
